messages:
incident-bot: SEV-2 Alert — KV cache resident set grew 3.8x above baseline in us-west-2 for continuous-batching pool (mqa models). Grafana: <https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv-cache> :rotating_light:

alex: oncall here, looking. seeing steady growth starting ~10m ago. latency spike for 8k+ token requests. attaching flamegraph.

alex: maya, you free? this looks like continuous-batching + prefix reuse blowup. model mix: llama-mqa-v1 + qwen-mqa-v2 on same pool.

maya: I'm on. digging into prefix map eviction logs. preliminary: prefetch + MQA prefix collisions caused unbounded KV entries for some long-prefix traces. suspect batch window + prefetch enabled both contributing.

liam: I see repeated keys for the same prefix across sessions: key churn correlates with continuous-batch group size. eviction not keeping up because k/v count >> configured max_entries.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefetch for mqa families (set prefetch.enabled=false) 2) drop batch window from 50ms -> 20ms 3) increase eviction aggressiveness (kv.max_entries -> 120M) 4) if needed, fallback route traffic to compatible gqa variant.

alex: can we do 1+2 quickly? I'm worried about rollback risk for 3.

maya: yes. pushing a control-plane config change now for prefetch toggle and batch window. command:

```bash
curl -XPOST https://controlplane.redwood.example/api/v1/configs/pools/continuous-batching -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' -d '{"prefetch.enabled":false, "batch.window_ms":20}'
```

maya: deployed config patch -> 2246007925. Applying to us-west-2 shard group.

incident-bot: Deploy event: config-change by maya at 2246007925 (continuous-batching pool).

alex: monitoring graphs. cache growth plateaued, >30% reduction in new entries within 90s. latency dropping on tail p95 for 8k tokens.

liam: logs show eviction doing more work but catching up. still seeing some hot shards with high mem usage. recommend restarting one affected worker to reclaim memory.

maya: agreed. doing a rolling restart of worker nodes in the hottest shard with graceful drain. command: `infractl drain --shard us-west-2-shard-7 && infractl restart node-7`

sara: CS: tally on customer impact — initial telemetry shows error rate rose from 0.4% -> 2.9% for long-context requests between 2246007200-2246007900. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream for some enterprise customers using long-history prompts. I will open customer tickets and send a sourcemap to affected accounts.

priya: product note — we saw this in staging with a particular prompt pattern (repeated role tokens + long system prefix). adding eval to guard against unbounded prefix reuse. file created: internal/alerts/prompt-pattern-guard.md

alex: restart completed on node-7 at 2246008100. memory reclaimed. p99 latency back to baseline for most routes but p95 still slightly elevated for 12 tenants.

maya: after restart and config change, cache growth returned to stable baseline. we'll keep prefetch disabled for mqa family for 24h and observe. opening a follow-up RFC for better eviction heuristics and model-aware prefetch.

liam: short-term hotfix note for runbook: if cache growth detected >2x baseline AND prefetch.enabled=true -> flip prefetch off, lower batch.window_ms to 20, consider shard restart. Add these commands to runbook.

alex: handoff: I'm handing pager to maya for the next 3h while I finish post-incident log collection. i'm putting this on-call to-do in the incident tracker.

maya: taking pager. will watch for 2h stable window then hand back. I'll also coordinate with eng-runtime to create a canary to simulate the prompt pattern and validate the RFC.

sara: CS update: initial outreach email drafted, waiting on severity confirmation. impact estimate: ~12 customers with transient increased latency/errors, no PII exposure, no data loss.

priya: tagging research — we should investigate model-level kv key namespaces to avoid cross-model collisions (mqa/gqa differences). adding a note to model-onboarding checklist.

alex: retrospective owner: liam (eviction heuristics), priya (onboarding checklist), maya (runtime config & automation).

incident-bot: Incident updated to declared mitigated at 2246008680. postmortem required: yes. severity: S2.

maya: quick timeline summary to attach to incident:
- 2246007200: first anomaly detection (metrics threshold)
- 2246007285: pager triggered
- 2246007350: initial ack by alex
- 2246007925: prefetch disabled + batch window lowered (hotfix)
- 2246008100: rolling restart hot shard node-7
- 2246008680: mitigated (metrics stable)

alex: thanks team. going to cut a short incident note for customer-facing comms and link the postmortem once ready. please add any logs/commands to the incident thread. :thumbsup:

maya: will follow up with a short runbook PR and the RFC link. leaving monitoring hooks in the console.

liam: added a Grafana alert tweak to reduce noise but catch this pattern earlier.

sara: CS: sending notices now. will request any affected customers to share request IDs if they need deeper traces.

priya: adding model-onboarding guard as an action item.

alex: handoff complete. maya you have the pager. I'll remain reachable.

maya: acknowledged. monitoring.

cs-bot: Ticket created: INC-2246007890-cs-outreach (sara).

alex: closing thread for now, leave notes if anything else crops up.

maya: will post the postmortem draft in #postmortems by EOD.
